Hi everyone, Quantum computing is the most talked-about long-term threat to Bitcoin right now, and most of what you’re reading about it is either FUD or hand-waving. Below I’ve written out my classic long-form article, but if you’d rather watch a video, here is the video link. Below I’ll cover what quantum actually breaks, how many coins are exposed, how close the machines are, the two BIPs everyone is fighting about, and where I land. At the end there’s a 5-step checklist, including the one address type I’d stop using for long-term savings. Overview There are two main issues with upgrading Bitcoin to post-quantum: The upgrade itself: how to technically upgrade Bitcoin in time The old coins: what to do with coins that haven’t moved after the migration I’ve been in Bitcoin since 2012, and I’ve always looked at the protocol through its three core value props: the hardest monetary policy in history, an asset that’s extraordinarily difficult to seize, and a censorship-resistant ability to send money. Quantum computing is a real long-term risk to the second one. But it’s not the apocalyptic FUD some people portray. It’s a solvable engineering problem that needs calm, rational discussion now. What quantum breaks (and what it doesn’t) What it breaks: your wallet/private key. Shor’s algorithm on a big enough quantum computer turns a public key into a private key. What it doesn’t break: mining or the 21M cap. Adam Back put it simply: “quantum computers are NOT good at attacking hash functions. attacking bitcoin’s PoW is not the thing to focus on - it’s ECDSA.” (Aug 3, 2026) There are two kinds of attack: Long exposure (coins at rest): the public key is already on-chain, so the attacker has unlimited time. Short exposure (coins in transit): your public key sits in the mempool until it confirms, about 10 minutes on average. Long-exposure ones get hit first because a quantum computer can take all the time it needs to crack the keys. How much BTC is exposed? As of May 20, 2026, 6.04M BTC, or 30.2% of issued supply, has a visible public key. Other counts run higher: Project Eleven has ~6.8M BTC (Google’s paper cites ~6.9M) (Bitcoin Risq List). And the number that matters most for the Satoshi debate: Jameson Lopp estimates at least 2.6M BTC (about 13% of supply) would stay vulnerable even if every active user migrated to post-quantum secure cryptography (Bitcoin Magaz

82416.subject:
The New York Stock Exchange Puts Avalanche at the Core of Its Tokenized
 Securities Platform
82416.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/the-new-york-stock-exchange-puts

The New York Stock Exchange has decided to put Avalanche at the center of its new infrastructure for tokenized equities and 24/7 trading. Avalanche will provide the core ledger technology for the upcoming NYSE-affiliated tokenized securities platform. According to the Wall Street Journal [ https://substack.com/redirect/65da08a1-bfe2-442e-99f4-04a359858eab?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], NYSE said it will settle tokenized stocks on the platform exclusively on Avalanche.
Charley Cooper, President and COO of Ava Labs, explained what that means in an interview [ https://substack.com/redirect/ab2a5e5c-0e87-4d47-82fb-fd07fc2ec016?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] on NYSE Live. Most of what he described happens after a trade is made, and that is where this announcement matters.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
The part of a trade most people never see
A trade starts with issuance and a match. Then comes a long list of steps that NYSE knows well and most traders never think about, such as clearing, settlement, and cash collateral. These steps normally take time and leave capital trapped while they finish. By putting Avalanche at the core of the platform, they happen instantly.
NYSE’s own technology will keep matching trades, and Avalanche will settle them.
Why 24/7 trading depends on it
Many exchanges around the world want to move to round-the-clock markets but trading all night only helps if everything after the trade keeps up. A trade made in the middle of the night or over a weekend has little value if settlement and clearing cannot keep pace.
Without this kind of infrastructure, a move to 24/7 markets would be much harder to deliver. According to Cooper, this is why the announcement is a milestone for the equities industry as well as for blockchain. ICE, NYSE’s parent, has said it is preparing its own clearing infrastructure to support 24/7 trading.
What makes this different from other onchain efforts
There are two main aspects that differentiate the platform:
The first is where the work is happening. People got excited about tokenizing equities, but putting an asset onchain does little on its own. The gains come downstream, in the post-trade steps. Cooper described those gains as efficiency, better use of capital, and the release of assets that would otherwise be trapped.
The second is the intent. Many pilots and proofs of concept have run in the industry for years. This one is aimed at production. When NYSE is ready, and its regulators have approved it, the plan is to make 24/7 trading live and open to the market, rather than keeping it in a test environment.

Welcome to the third edition of Inside Spiko, our monthly roundup of what's new, and what it actually means for you. On the agenda: Our $90 million Series B, led by NEA and Index Ventures Product news: the Spiko app on iOS and Android, Smart Cash in Swiss francs with Spiko Franc, and an aggregated view of all your entities Spiko by the numbers: how many withdrawals happen outside banking hours, plus our current net yields The macro picture: the Bank of England raises rates, and what markets expect from the ECB and the Fed in December Enjoy the read! Spiko raises $90 million On October 6, we announced a $90 million Series B led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and Index Ventures. Axel Weber, former president of the Bundesbank, and the founders of Qonto also took part in the round. In total, Spiko has raised $120 million since it was founded. What this means for you: new products, new markets and a bigger team to support you. Our mission stays the same: making your treasury work for you, as efficiently as possible. Thank you: we owe this milestone first and foremost to your trust. Read our blog post on the round 1. Product news Spiko goes mobile The Spiko app is available on iOS and Android. You can manage all your operations there: deposits, withdrawals, transfers between accounts. More than 6,500 users have already adopted it, and nearly 700 opened their Spiko account entirely from their phone. The app also makes your account more secure: Face ID to log in Your phone as a two-step verification factor to approve sensitive actions (withdrawals, adding a beneficiary, etc.) Two-step verification at login: turn this option on in your settings to add a check after your password.
